The Project

Two slender towers, one podium

CloutHaus rises on one of the last parcels of land facing the Petronas Twin Towers — the developer's own description, and the reason the whole scheme is organised around the view.

Two towers stand above a shared podium whose gentle curvature the brochure likens to an unfolding curtain. Menara 1 runs to 58 storeys and 242 residences; Tower 2 runs to 66 storeys and 615 — 857 homes in total, on freehold land with no encumbrance and no restriction in interest.

It is built by TA First Credit Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of TA Global Bhd, from Menara TA One a few doors away. Day-to-day the building is serviced by Paradox Hotels & Resorts, so the residences carry hotel services rather than a management office.

  • Freehold, with no encumbrance and no restriction in interest
  • On a parcel facing the Petronas Twin Towers
  • Hotel services by Paradox Hotels & Resorts
  • Two towers of 66 and 58 storeys, 857 serviced residences
  • 549 to 2,427 sq ft — including one-bedroom homes over 1,000 sq ft
  • Expected completion January 2029

The Layout Thesis

The square feet go where you actually live

Read the layout schedule and something unusual shows up: CloutHaus builds one-bedroom homes at sizes most projects reserve for three. The space goes into living, dining and entertaining instead of extra rooms.

One bedroomTwo or three bedrooms

Type M is a one-bedroom at 1,173 sq ft. Type I is a three-bedroom at 1,119 sq ft. The one-bedroom is the larger of the two. Six of the eleven drawn layouts are one-bedroom homes, and four of those are over 890 sq ft.

The Sky Floors

Everything shared is up in the air

The pool, the lounge and the trellis deck all sit high in the towers and all face the same direction. The brochure calls it a curated retreat in the sky; in practice it means the amenity looks at the Twin Towers rather than at the podium roof.

Before You Ask

The questions that come up first

In Kuala Lumpur City Centre, on a parcel facing the Petronas Twin Towers. The developer describes it as one of the last parcels of land facing the towers. The sales gallery is on the Mezzanine Floor of Menara TA One, 22 Jalan P. Ramlee, 50250 Kuala Lumpur. The brochure maps the surrounding landmarks but publishes no distances, so this page quotes none — ask me and I'll measure the ones you care about.
This page deliberately doesn't print a figure. At this level the price turns on the tower, the floor and the facing, it moves with the stock that is left, and the two towers are priced on separate schedules — a single range on a web page would mislead more than it helps. Message me and I'll send the current price list for both towers with the payment structure, and confirm anything you may be eligible for.
Freehold, per the advertising permit, with land encumbrance: NIL and restriction in interest: NIL. That is unusual for a new high-rise this close to KLCC and it is one of the harder facts in the brochure.
Two towers on a shared podium. Menara 1 is 58 storeys with 242 residences; Tower 2 is 66 storeys with 615 — 857 homes in total. At the permit date the balance was 242 and 611 respectively. Development type is Serviced Residences.
Tower 2. The eleven layouts drawn above match the Tower 2 schedule in the permit exactly. Menara 1 has its own type letters and its own sizes — its Type A is 174 sq m against Tower 2's 113 sq m — and the brochure prints no plans for them. So "Type A" means two different homes depending on the tower. If you want Menara 1, tell me and I'll get that schedule directly.
Read this one carefully. On the Tower 2 schedule every single-unit type is listed with 0 car-park bays; only the combined types G-G, H-G and I-G carry 1 bay each. On Menara 1, types A, B and I carry 2 bays, G and H carry 1, and C to F carry 0. If a bay is essential, that narrows the shortlist a lot — say so up front and I'll only show you units that have one.
Because the plans put the space into living rather than bedrooms. Six of the eleven drawn layouts are one-bedroom homes, and four of those are over 890 sq ft — Type N at 893, Type J at 1,001, Type B at 1,098 and Type M at 1,173 sq ft, which is larger than the 1,119 sq ft three-bedroom Type I. They are built around a long living-dining run, a full kitchen and two bathrooms, which suits a city base or a home for entertaining more than a household with children.
The brochure states international branded hotel services by Paradox Hotel Group, and the back cover carries "Serviced by Paradox Hotels & Resorts". It does not publish the service list, the operating agreement or the service charge, so this page does not describe them — those are questions for the developer and I'll put them in writing for you.
The brochure captions a Sky Pool, a Sky Lounge and its deck, a Sky Trellis Lounge, a Sky BBQ with a Kids Pool, and a Games Room. It does not print a numbered facility schedule or the levels they sit on, so neither does this page. Ask me for the floor-by-floor list.
The permit gives an expected date of completion of January 2029. Building plan approval is BP T3 OSC 2011 1684 and the approving authority is Dewan Bandaraya Kuala Lumpur.
The developer is TA First Credit Sdn Bhd (197601003011 / 29009-A), a subsidiary of TA Global Bhd (200801027528 / 828855-P), which is the holding company of TA Properties Sdn Bhd (199101005140 / 215450-W). Their registered address is the 34th Floor, Menara TA One, 22 Jalan P. Ramlee, 50250 Kuala Lumpur — the same building as the sales gallery.
Straight answer: the permit printed on this brochure has lapsed. Advertising & Sales Permit 9149-2/07-2025/0576(R)-(S) was valid 31/07/2024 to 30/07/2025. The developer's licence 9149/07-2027/0768(A) runs to 30/07/2027 and is current. The footer prints both exactly as the brochure does and no number has been substituted. I've asked for the renewed permit; when it comes through it is a one-line change here.
